about: IP / VLAN / DNS plan for VCF 9.1 and later: which components need an FQDN and a static IP on the management network, reserved ranges, and how much room subnets get.

records.source: Broadcom TechDocs, VCF 9.1: First VCF Instance FQDNs and IP Addresses; Network Deployment Options for VCF Components
records.notes: Every VCF component needs a unique FQDN and a static IP with forward (A) and reverse (PTR) DNS; no capital letters in FQDNs; containerized services don't support .local domains. All these addresses are on the VCF management network, which by default shares the VM management network. Counts are the page's simple / HA columns. Fleet-level components are placed in the first instance; the additional-instance page hasn't been checked yet, so later instances list only per-instance components. VCF Operations data node: HA with medium or large only. Edge node management IPs: static, per the host fault tolerant edge cluster design (RCMD-COMSAZ-016).

reserved.source: Broadcom TechDocs, VCF 9.1: First VCF Instance FQDNs and IP Addresses (services runtime CIDR); IPv4 Addressing Model (inter-tier transit)
reserved.notes: VCF services runtime uses the internal 198.18.0.0/15 (minimum 12, recommended 30 addresses per runtime); if it's in use on your network it must be changed at deployment. NSX inter-tier transit links use a subset of 100.64.0.0/10 (RFC 6598).

sizing.source: VCF Design Studio default: subnets get room for twice today's addresses, because VCF can't change an infrastructure subnet's mask later (VCF-NET-RCMD-IPA-001). Tier-0 peering /28 (VCF-WLDCON-CTGW-RCMD-CFG-009).
